feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV for a senior digital communications role: clear positioning, credible progression, and solid evidence of leadership in web, content, analytics, and multimedia. It reads polished and substantive, though it would be stronger with tighter formatting consistency, fewer repeated themes, and more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope/activity.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility and credibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong strategic profile with relevant technical depth; the mix of Drupal, analytics, governance, and multimedia supports the “Digital Communications & Strategy Lead” brand well.  
- Writing is generally clean, professional, and easy to follow, with good use of specifics such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact/results language: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, conversions, adoption, or cost/time savings.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and dilute impact. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); keep punctuation/bullet formatting uniform across sections.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads a bit generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it around your most relevant differentiators—platform modernization, advocacy/public-sector communications, and operational leadership—would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with higher-value positioning tied to leadership and transformation.
- Add public-sector/association context to align with the NACo-heavy experience.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial operations, analytics, and digital governance, with a strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused communications. Experienced in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and developing the systems and workflows that enable scalable content operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- The multimedia emphasis is already well covered in Work Experience and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it sharper and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with more senior, distinctive language: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” “Editorial systems & governance” instead of “Editorial workflow design.”
- Align wording with the strongest evidence in experience: web platform modernization, cross-channel communications leadership, analytics/insights, advocacy messaging, and multimedia production.
- Use parallel noun phrases and consistent style throughout.

Suggested rewrite:
Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization & CMS administration • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination • Policy and advocacy communications • Multimedia and live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” duplicates the header and Topline Skills; “cross-channel communications leadership” is stronger.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills; keep only if this section remains high-level.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and technical depth, but it reads a bit list-like and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below. Tighten around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and 2–3 signature contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, and web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate bullets around impact themes: digital systems/workflows, Drupal campaign builds, governance/usability, and AI search leadership.
- Replace generic verbs (“build and refine,” “deliver,” “advise”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “streamlined,” “designed,” “implemented,” “launched,” “defined.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/pages, users, teams supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search performance gains, publishing efficiency improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording repeats themes already covered in “Director of Digital Media” (web improvement, analytics, governance, Drupal). Emphasize consulting/advisory capacity and new initiatives since Jun. 2024.
- The microsite and AI search bullets may duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the build details.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational leadership, and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Led NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Directed redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific and measurable: include email volume/open-rate growth, audience growth, engagement, or campaign impact if available; otherwise trim “tens of thousands/thousands.”
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built analytics and governance infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video/studio language may overlap with the footer project list; keep this bullet centered on building in-house production capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and solid scope, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify what you built or scaled before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy distribution during a period of organizational growth.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show creation and adoption: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make workflow/editorial bullets more concrete if possible: add examples or metrics such as publishing volume, turnaround time, campaign cadence, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning…” and “improved…publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager / Producer entry; distinguish this role by emphasizing scale, coordination, and channel ownership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior positioning and emphasize enterprise/public-sector scope rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, higher-signal phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and information design
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Enterprise web governance” if you want stronger alignment with recent leadership roles.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g., “Content operations for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than the operational strengths shown in recent roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution strengths rather than listing every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, impact-oriented line: **Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences**
- Remove lower-priority or older/platform-specific items here if they are not central to recent work: **WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, jQuery**
- Use broader phrasing in this section and leave exact tools/frameworks to “Technical + IT”
- If you want one stronger differentiator, replace “CMS modernization” with **Drupal migrations and large-site platform modernization**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of **Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS** and **Coding & Technical Implementation**
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies; keep it in only one place unless it is a signature strength

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This Topline Skills item should emphasize strategic analytics leadership, not repeat the stack.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • User behavior analysis • SEO and performance optimization”
- Keep only 2–3 flagship tools here and move the full stack to Technical + IT; e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “Executive reporting” or “Board/leadership dashboarding”
- If space allows, tie to impact language: “Measurement frameworks that improved decision-making across web, campaign and content operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current tool list duplicates the Technical + IT “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may partially overlap with broader digital strategy language elsewhere; keep this item focused on measurement and insight.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo role bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, more distinctive capabilities rather than generic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership + delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match recent director-level work.
- Consider dropping “virtual” if “hybrid event delivery” already covers it; this saves space and sounds more current.
- If accurate, add scale/complexity in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., studio buildout, recurring programming, or event support volume.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and video capability are already supported by the Director of Digital Media bullets, so this skills line should stay concise and differentiated.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since recent experience is strongly Drupal-centered, the item should emphasize depth/relevance rather than read as a generic platform inventory.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider adding light qualifiers: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**.
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented rather than just a list: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use **CMS & Web Platforms** or **CMS Platforms** for a cleaner heading.
- If GitHub Pages was only occasional use, move it to Coding/Technical Implementation and keep this item focused on primary CMS platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” especially Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles and projects; avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context or scale.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support your recent Drupal/AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as applied capabilities, not just languages/tools: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more senior.
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., integrations supporting analytics, search, or campaign microsites.
- Put the most current/distinctive items first: “Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • JavaScript • HTML/CSS • jQuery”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- GTM may also fit under Analytics/Optimization if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation leadership. Since automation and planning systems already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to improve scanability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Remove weaker/older tools unless recently used; prioritize platforms tied to current work, especially Airtable, Power Automate, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: “Workflow automation and team operations tools: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello overlap heavily; listing all four may feel redundant unless each reflects meaningful recent use.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership is already established in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/enterprise weight: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional context instead of only names: **Higher Logic (member email/community) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation/segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**
- Keep punctuation/style consistent with other technical items; avoid slashes if possible: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated email-channel references in Work Experience; don’t add claims like “managed newsletters” here.
- “Engagement” may imply CRM/community ownership; only keep that label if you directly administered these systems.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” or scale to distinguish it from the 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows spanning web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten the second sentence around distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate.”
- Replace soft phrases like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with measurable or operational language.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the next role; keep it here only if you frame this role as launching or first establishing the series.
- Team-building/workflow language also appears in later NACo roles; avoid repeating governance/operations phrasing.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination scope and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; helped translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add scale: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders/program teams served, or audience/download growth.
- Remove “contributed to” language where you had ownership; use stronger verbs like “developed,” “produced,” or “launched.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production and multimedia materials,” which is covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Keep this entry focused on innovation/research support + first podcast, not general digital operations.
